title: Free True Soul Nere
html:
Free True Soul Nere is a Quest in Act One of Baldur's Gate 3. It can be started when the party arrives at Grymforge and talks to  Sergeant Thrinn or after making a deal with Elder Brithvar.

“
So, are we saving this 'Nere' from suffocating or leaving him to die? I'm fine with either, naturally. The last thing I want is to ruin these nails digging through rock.
„
— Astarion, on the question of whether to rescue Nere

Objectives

Objectives and journal entries may vary pending story decisions and outcomes.

Clear the cave-in.
  • "Sergeant Thrinn said the True-Soul leading them is trapped behind the cave-in. She wants us to clear it."
  • "The deep gnomes are worried about Beldron. He's trapped with True Soul Nere behind the cave-in."
  • "We discovered several duergar who are plotting against Nere. They asked us to free him, and offered a cut of the prize if we help."
  • "We found some explosives. Let's see if it's enough to clear the cave-in."
  • "We found some rubble and were able to clear it. We should do the same for the cave-in."
  • "We managed to clear some but not all of the rubble."
  • "We used other methods to clear the rubble. Perhaps this could come in handy again."
  • "True Soul Nere warned us about the poisonous gas behind the cave-in. He'll die soon - we can't afford to rest."
Speak to Nere.
  • "We managed to clear the cave-in. Let's see what Nere has to say for himself."
Defeat the mutinous duergar.
  • "The duergar turned on Nere. We need to protect him."
Speak to Nere.
  • "The duergar were defeated. We should check on Nere."
Quest Complete
  • "The cave-in was cleared without our help."
  • "Nere mentioned that he's planning to go to the temple where he'll pick up the trail of Balthazar, the General's advisor."
  • "We revealed the truth to Nere - that the Absolute is a front for mind flayers. He gave us a token of his thanks."
  • "We turned on Nere."
  • "Nere is dead."
  • "We left Grymforge without clearing the cave-in."
  • "We left Grymforge - leaving Nere to his fate."

Walkthrough

This quest is on a "timer", tracked by long rests or fast travels. The timer starts when a party member speaks with  Nere by interacting with the rubble. After this, a warning in the form of a cutscene with Nere is triggered upon the party's arrival in camp the first time after they enter Grymforge. The quest can fail if they long rest or fast travel after it is started. The party can also let the timer run out and have Nere die prior to freeing him as an alternative way to solve the quest ⁠Deliver Nere's Head.

Arriving at Grymforge

The quest to free Nere is initiated the first time the party takes the boat in the Decrepit Village to Grymforge. During the trip over, a group of duergar on another boat led by  Corsair Greymon questions the player character on what they are doing on  Gekh Coal's boat:

[1]
  • [DECEPTION] I saw a body left by the myconids - your 'Gekh' must be dead. (DC 10) (if Gekh Coal unmet)
  • [DECEPTION] I'm afraid Gekh is dead - he fell fighting the myconids (DC 10) (if Gekh Coal was met)
  • [BRANDED] [PERSUASION] Just let me cross - I have the brand, see? (DC 10)
  • I work on Gekh's behalf. I'm after his sergeant's stolen boots. (if quest started to find the boots)
  • I seek the sergeant - I believe she's keen to get these boots back. (if boots quest was not started)
  • [BERSERKER] [INTIMIDATION] MOVE YOUR BOAT, OR SINK. MAKE THE CHOICE. (DC 10 )
  • [INTIMIDATION] In the name of the Absolute - you will let me pass. (DC 10)
  • [ATHLETICS] Push the duergar into the water. (DC 15)

Duergar characters have slightly easier DCs:

[1]
  • [DECEPTION] I saw a body left by the myconids - your 'Gekh' must be dead. (DC 5) (if Gekh Coal unmet)
  • [DECEPTION] I'm afraid Gekh is dead - he fell fighting the myconids (DC 5) (if Gekh Coal was met)
  • [BRANDED] [PERSUASION] Just let me cross - I have the brand, see? (DC 5)

...while Dwarf characters have much harder DCs:

[1]
  • [DECEPTION] Duergar, like you? Saw his body a way back. Myconids got him. (DC 20) (if Gekh Coal unmet)
  • [DECEPTION] I'm afraid Gekh is dead. He fell fighting the myconids. (DC 20) (if Gekh Coal was met)
  • [BRANDED] [PERSUASION] See this brand? Let me pass. (DC 15)

Succeeding the check results in the Corsair standing down and telling the party to speak with Sergeant Thrinn. If he is pushed into the water during the cut-scene his body irretrievably sinks to the botton of the water and a fight breaks out, earning  +5 and  +1 approval. The corpses of any characters shoved off of the boats during combat wash up on the beach at the Decrepit Village afterward.

Once docked, another duergar,  Morghal, tries to extort money from the player character. Telling her "I’m not giving you a single coin" results in her backing off immediately. The party must follow the path south to come across a cave-in, where a group of enslaved gnomes are being forced to chip away at the rocks at X: -635 Y: 311. Speaking to Sergeant Thrinn reveals that Nere, a drow and True Soul, is trapped by a cave-in.

Communicating with Nere

If a party member interacts with the cave-in, Nere telepathically connects with them and shows what he sees. If they pass a  DC 10 Perception Check to try to focus on what Nere can see, the interacting party member sees two gnomes on his side of the cave-in who are trying to remove rocks, as well as two dead gnomes who were killed by a magical trap. The player character also senses Nere's frustration and rage before the connection fades.

The cave-in

The primary objective of this quest is to destroy the caved-in wall of debris trapping Nere. The pile of rocks has 44 Hit Points and is immune to all types of damage except for force (vulnerable), piercing (resistant) and bludgeoning. It also has the  Medium Toughness condition - a hit must deal 22 or more damage to damage it.

There several ways to destroy the cave-in. Due to its vulnerability to force, explosives such as  Smokepowder Satchel or  Smokepowder Bomb are viable solutions. However, sufficient force, or bludgeoning damage from abilities can also work - such as high rolls on a Warlock's  Eldritch Blast combined with the cave-in's force vulnerability, or melee attacks with high strength, Great Weapon Master: All In using a Maul. Finally,  Tavern Brawlers can use thrown weapons to destroy the cave in.

Placing any explosive object onto the floor (i.e., dropping it) should make all the digging gnomes scramble away, saving them from taking damage. However, after the rubble is cleared, Thrinn may run towards Nere. Should she take damage from any residual fire surface, the dialogue is skipped, and combat begins with all duergar and Nere. This risk can be mitigated by switching to turn-based mode, and targeting the fire surface with cold damage before Thrinn reaches it.[2]

The party can obtain enough explosives to complete this quest by solving the ⁠Find the Explosives quest, also located at Grymforge.

Successfully removing the caved-in rubble initiates a cutscene with Nere, which directly affects the quest ⁠Save the Grymforge Gnomes.

The mutiny

Upon being freed Nere is furious at being trapped and immediately takes it out on  Meerna who he casts into the lava.

If the player character chooses to say nothing or "Finish the slaves, True Soul. For the Absolute", then Nere massacres all the gnomes. If the player character tells Nere not to kill innocents, he tells Thrinn to rip out their heart and feed it to the Deep Rothé. At this point, if the party made a deal with Brithvar to kill Nere, he interjects saying that Nere owes the duergar money and he is going to get it from his corpse. Seething at this betrayal, Nere then says that he has changed his mind and will spare the party if they defeat Brithvar and the other mutineers.

If the party sides with Nere, they must fight against:

  •  Brithvar
  •  Kur
  •  Morghal
  •  Orgarth
  •  Mirthis
  •  Danna
  •  Thudd

If the party sides with Brithvar, they must fight against:

  •  Nere
  •  Elenna Thrinn
  •  Dalthar
  •  Drar
  •  Greymon
  •  Fonmara
  •  Dunnol

Siding with Nere

If Nere is sided with, there are two distinct paths which can be followed. One is where Nere tells the party to travel to  Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers. The other is Nere being informed by the party that the Cult of the Absolute is a front for mind flayers, in which case he abandons the cult entirely.

After the battle, Nere says that the Absolute's business is unfinished. If the player character selects either "Unfortunate - but how does this concern me?" or "And what business is that, exactly?", he then bids them to tell the General that he did what he could, but the route through Grymforge is impassable. If they select "I'll do it. Where can I find the General?", Nere then explains that the party must travel through the Shadow-Cursed Lands. He had a Moonlantern which could ward off the shadow curse, but it was destroyed in the cave-in. If player character asks "If that's the case, how do I reach it safely?", Nere reveals there is a guide who will appear when they play the  Spider's Lyre he provides.

The divergence occurs based on what the player character says next. If they say "I'd rather make my own way than rely on your help." then Nere says the Absolute should be demanding that he takes the player character's head for such insolence, but he cannot hear her voice. Choosing the option "Explain that the Absolute is a front for mind flayers - you're protected from them." starts Nere on the path where he may falter from the Absolute:

[3]
  • [DECEPTION] It's true - it's a shadowy conspiracy headed by mind flayers and... tax collectors. (DC 10)
  • [PERSUASION] I was abducted by mind flayers. That was when I began to hear the Absolute. (DC 10)

Nere then needs one more push to abandon the cult:

[3]
  • Your faith in Lolth faltered. It is not too late to reclaim it. (Lolth-sworn drow only)
  • [PERSUASION] You don't have to. Run - abandon the Absolute. (DC 10)
  • [HISTORY] People have followed cults for a long time. You're just another victim. (DC 10)
  • [DETECT THOUGHTS] [WISDOM] Cast Detect Thoughts
    • Your faith in Lolth faltered. It is not too late to reclaim it.

If he is convinced, Nere says dying for mind flayer filth is not worth it. He thanks the player character for saving him from something worse than the duergar. After rewarding the party, he leaves and prays that he does not meet them again.

Related quests

  • ⁠Blind the Absolute
  • ⁠Deliver Nere's Head
  • ⁠Find Explosives
  • ⁠Rescue Wulbren
  • ⁠Save the Grymforge Gnomes

Quest rewards

If Nere is sided with and abandons the cult:

  • Dagger +1

If Nere is sided with and remains in the cult:

  • Gift from the Absolute

If Brithvar is sided with:

  • 400 gold (or 500 gold if convinced earlier to give half the spoils)
  • ⁠Perfect Cut for party members with the  Criminal background

Loot from Nere if he is killed:

  • 1000 gold
  • Broken Moonlantern
  • Disintegrating Night Walkers
  • Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen
  • Nere's Head (conditional, see item page)
  • Sword of Screams

It is possible to get both  Gift from the Absolute and  Mind Flayer Parasite Specimen by first completing the quest then killing Nere later.

Companion approval

  • Standing up for the deep gnome slaves after Nere is freed  -1  +1  +1  +1
  • After rescuing Nere, tell him to finish the slaves, or saying nothing  +1  +1
  • Siding with Brithvar when confronting Nere  -1  +1 +1
  • Siding with Nere against Brithvar  -5  -1
  • Letting Brithvar take the deep gnomes  -1

Notes

  1. ↑ 1.0 1.1 1.2 Dialogue file: Act1/Underdark/UND_DarkLake_RaftEvent
  2. ↑ Testing has shown that using water to extinguish the fire surface sometimes leads to electrified steam, which has the same result as a fire surface.
  3. ↑ 3.0 3.1 Dialogue file: Act1/Underdark/UND_TheDrowNere_FollowUp

Bugs

  • When the party side with Nere, just after the fight against Elder Brithvar, a conversation is supposed to begin automatically with Nere. However, a bug can occur during the fight, which causes the conversation to not trigger. This can be confirmed if the quest asks to talk with Nere, but in doing so, his response is "Leave me be. You've done enough." and nothing happens. As of patch 6, the bug is still present in the game. There is no known solution other than loading a save before the fight and redoing it.
  • If the party use an explosive that causes a fire surface near the rubble, and the rubble is not cleared from the first such explosion, the gnomes can walk over the fire surface and take damage; this provokes the start of a battle, as if the party had attacked the gnomes.
